assumptions: No conjecture is needed for a lower-bound certificate.
GRH is relevant only to the published assertion that the rank-29 curve has no thirtieth generator; that upper bound is not used here.
approaches.blocker: The primary fibration data and original scoring pipeline are not yet represented in a clean executable form on main.
approaches.central_mechanism: Specialize a large generic Mordell-Weil subgroup and search for at least 13 additional independent rational points outside it.
approaches.computational_cost: High: symbolic reconstruction plus large specialization scans and deep point searches.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Recover the explicit fibration, parameter, 17 generic sections, specialization maps, and original scoring code from primary material; reproduce the rank-29 parameter and decompose its 29 certified points into 17 generic plus 12 exceptional directions. Then run prime-by-prime score ablations around that parameter.
evidence_against: A jump of 12 was already exceptional; a jump of 13 may be much rarer under the same distribution.
The explicit fibration and complete original search implementation have not yet been reconstructed on main.
Searching farther without identifying structural predictors would mostly buy a linear increase in trials.
evidence_for: The repository now has an unconditional exact rank-at-least-29 certificate for the published record curve.
The same K3 surface produced two consecutive records, indicating unusually productive geometry.
The 2024 specialization produced 12 directions outside the generic rank-17 subgroup.
approaches.mathematical_family: The rank-17 elliptic fibration on the K3 surface used for the 2006 rank-28 and 2024 rank-29 records.
approaches.missing_lemma: An interpretable arithmetic or geometric predictor for specializations carrying unusually many points outside the generic subgroup.
approaches.predicted_advantage: This is the only construction already demonstrated to reach rank 29, so the required improvement is one additional direction on a proven search landscape.

approaches.blocker: The exact Neron-Severi lattice and automorphism action of the record model have not yet been reconstructed.
approaches.central_mechanism: Use Neron-Severi lattice calculations, neighbor steps, automorphisms, and alternative pencils to raise generic rank or lower section/coefficient heights before specialization.
approaches.computational_cost: High symbolic cost, followed by medium-to-high arithmetic verification cost.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Reconstruct the singular-fiber configuration and a Gram matrix for the Neron-Severi lattice; enumerate admissible primitive U-embeddings and 2-neighbor/3-neighbor fibrations; compute the Shioda-Tate upper bound and rationality of candidate sections for each orbit.
evidence_against: A high geometric rank need not descend to Q.
Alternative fibrations may dramatically increase coefficient complexity or section heights.
No explicit fibration better than the rank-17 record fibration is yet verified here.
evidence_for: A high-Picard-rank K3 generally admits many inequivalent elliptic fibrations.
The record surface already supports an unusually large Mordell-Weil lattice.
approaches.mathematical_family: Alternative elliptic fibrations on the record K3 surface and closely related high-Picard-rank K3 surfaces.
approaches.missing_lemma: An explicit rational fibration whose expected total cost to rank 30 improves on the current record fibration.
approaches.predicted_advantage: Raising the generic floor from 17 to 18 or more can be more valuable than orders of magnitude of additional scans in the original fibration.

approaches.blocker: The record fibration's quadratic multisections have not yet been enumerated in a form suitable for the packet audit.
approaches.central_mechanism: Two independent squareclasses can expose a third product-character section while the composite cover remains genus zero, adding three independent directions rather than two.
approaches.computational_cost: Medium for squareclass/branch audits; high if complete Mordell-Weil searches on product twists are required.
approaches.concrete_next_test: For every pair of quadratic multisections in a high-rank family, compute valuation-parity vectors, enumerate all three nontrivial character twists, search the product twist for a section, and retain only packets whose composite cover has genus zero or one.
evidence_against: The displayed example certifies only three generic directions and is not itself close to rank 30.
A suitable packet has not yet been found inside the record rank-17 fibration.
evidence_for: research/packet3_certificate.py proves an explicit degree-four genus-zero example with three non-torsion character sections.
certificates/packet3_certificate.json is recomputed successfully in CI using only exact standard-library arithmetic.
approaches.mathematical_family: Biquadratic base changes and the three nontrivial quadratic-character twists of an elliptic surface.
approaches.missing_lemma: Existence of a positive product-character section compatible with a high-generic-rank Q-rational fibration and low-genus composite base.
approaches.predicted_advantage: It converts hidden product-twist arithmetic into a systematic generic-rank increment and can be transplanted into an already high-rank surface.

approaches.blocker: Existing branch claims have not yet passed independent mathematical review.
approaches.central_mechanism: Construct a large Mordell-Weil lattice geometrically first, then choose a Q-rational realization and specialization with additional arithmetic points.
approaches.computational_cost: High symbolic and lattice cost; potentially high specialization cost.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Independently audit the split-E8 construction files on the research branch; for the first valid model, compute singular fibers, Picard constraints, explicit sections, height pairing, and fields of definition from scratch.
evidence_against: Root-lattice rank can be absorbed by reducible fibers instead of appearing in the Mordell-Weil group.
Splitting over an extension rather than Q would not meet the target.
No audited explicit model in this thread currently supplies a higher Q(t)-rank than the record family.
evidence_for: Large root lattices are natural constituents of Neron-Severi and Mordell-Weil lattices on elliptic K3 surfaces.
The research branch contains candidate split-E8 constructions and finite-field scanners, but they are not yet trusted.
approaches.mathematical_family: Elliptic K3 surfaces with split E8-type lattice contributions, Shioda-Inose structures, or related lattice-polarized surfaces.
approaches.missing_lemma: A Q-rational realization whose Mordell-Weil lattice retains enough split directions after accounting for reducible fibers.
approaches.predicted_advantage: E8 blocks supply many controlled lattice directions and may raise the generic floor instead of relying on a rare specialization jump.

approaches.blocker: No low-dimensional auxiliary variety with a verified path to 20 or more independent sections has yet emerged.
approaches.central_mechanism: Reverse the usual search: encode many desired points first, use symmetry and elimination to lower the dimension, and parameterize the resulting auxiliary variety.
approaches.computational_cost: Medium at small N; rapidly high for direct Groebner elimination at large N.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Start with symmetric point patterns x=plus/minus r_i on y^2=x^3+A*x+B, eliminate A and B, compute the dimension and singular locus for N=6,8,10, and identify recurrences or rational fibrations before increasing N.
evidence_against: Naive dimension counts become unfavorable quickly.
Symmetry-generated points may carry unavoidable linear dependencies.
No construction from this route currently exceeds established generic-rank families.
evidence_for: Each prescribed point condition is algebraic and amenable to Groebner, resultant, interpolation, and modular methods.
Symmetry can create low-degree auxiliary equations and built-in relations that are visible before expensive searches.
approaches.mathematical_family: Auxiliary varieties obtained by prescribing many rational x-coordinates and solving simultaneously for a Weierstrass model and square right-hand sides.
approaches.missing_lemma: A scalable algebraic pattern forcing many points while avoiding an equally large space of Mordell-Weil relations.
approaches.predicted_advantage: A successful parameterization would make many rational points generic rather than exceptional and would change the probability model of the search.

approaches.blocker: The visibility theorem and its connection to an explicit elliptic surface still require independent audit.
approaches.central_mechanism: Replace thirty separate point equations by one structured norm identity with at least thirty-one controlled zeros, then recover points and certify the single expected principal-divisor relation.
approaches.computational_cost: Medium for small prototypes; very high for the full 31-zero system without additional structure.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Audit and reprove the proposed Riemann-Roch visibility bound from the research branch; implement exact small-degree analogues of A(x)^2-R(x)B(x)^2=c*product(x-r_i), measure the relation rank, and determine whether the construction scales without forcing extra dependencies.
evidence_against: A principal divisor automatically creates at least one relation among visible point classes.
Solving the norm identity at the required degree may be as difficult as the original rank problem.
Independence after transferring the zeros to an elliptic curve is not automatic.
evidence_for: Norm equations offer a single global algebraic object whose zeros can encode many candidate points.
The branch contains a proposed 31-zero formulation and certificate, but it has not yet been independently accepted.
approaches.mathematical_family: Norm-form and divisor constructions that encode many rational zeros of one function on a double cover.
approaches.missing_lemma: A rationally parameterized or efficiently solvable norm family whose visible divisor classes retain rank at least 30 after all forced relations.
approaches.predicted_advantage: The representation trades a large collection of square conditions for a structured polynomial identity that can be attacked with interpolation, lattice reduction, modular lifting, and coding-style sparsity constraints.

approaches.blocker: No audited family from this class currently has competitive expected cost to rank 30.
approaches.central_mechanism: Use an arithmetic identity that produces several rational points simultaneously and then combine independent identities or base changes without collapsing their Mordell-Weil directions.
approaches.computational_cost: Medium for literature reconstruction and exact verification; high for broad specialization scans.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Collect the strongest verified Q(t)-families from Diophantine tuples and related identities, canonicalize them, recompute their generic sections and height matrices, and rank them by the remaining specialization jump and coefficient growth.
evidence_against: Known tuple families generally remain far below the rank-17 generic floor of the record K3 construction.
Points generated by the same identity can have hidden dependencies.
Coefficient growth can make specialization point searches prohibitively expensive.
evidence_for: Structured Diophantine identities have repeatedly produced high-rank families and many explicit sections.
The construction data are usually exact and amenable to independent verification.
approaches.mathematical_family: Elliptic curves from rational Diophantine tuples, quadratic forms, polynomial identities, and rational surfaces carrying many sections.
approaches.missing_lemma: A composition principle that combines several point-producing identities while preserving independence and low coefficient complexity.
approaches.predicted_advantage: These constructions provide explicit coordinates and often cheap exact point verification, making them suitable inputs to a certificate-first search funnel.

approaches.blocker: No such packet beyond the verified three-character module is currently instantiated in the record geometry.
approaches.central_mechanism: Use arithmetic structure to manufacture rational points in several character or isogeny components and use descent both as a search tool and as an early rigorous filter.
approaches.computational_cost: Medium for branch-code enumeration; high for Mordell-Weil and covering searches on many twists.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Extend the packet3 audit to three or more squareclasses subject to a genus budget; enumerate low-branch binary codes, test every character twist for sections, and benchmark 2-covering point search against direct search on the same specializations.
evidence_against: The genus of a multiquadratic base rises rapidly with branch support.
Large Selmer groups need not contain rational points.
Twist gains over an auxiliary function field must still specialize back to Q.
evidence_for: The verified packet3 theorem demonstrates an exact three-character gain.
Descent and covering methods are standard sources of rigorous rank information and hidden points.
approaches.mathematical_family: Quadratic/cubic twists, isogeny families, Selmer structures, and explicit covering curves.
approaches.missing_lemma: A low-genus multi-character packet with a large positive total twist rank embedded in a competitive high-rank family.
approaches.predicted_advantage: Character separation can prove independence cheaply, while coverings can find points invisible to bounded direct x-searches.

assumptions: Heuristic scores are used only for prioritization, never as rank certificates.
approaches.blocker: No normalized candidate database and no reproduced baseline score distribution yet exist on main.
approaches.central_mechanism: Use cheap local rejection, adaptive Frobenius/Mestre-Nagao scoring, root-number and congruence filters, bounded point search, coverings, and incremental exact independence tests in a measured multi-stage funnel.
approaches.computational_cost: Low-to-medium for infrastructure; potentially massive for production scans.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Define the canonical candidate schema and benchmark corpus; reproduce the rank-29 specialization and a control sample; record candidates per second, survivor fractions, point yield, and marginal predictive value of every prime and filter.
evidence_against: The repository does not yet contain a clean reconstruction of the original scanner or a benchmark dataset.
Optimizing raw throughput without ablations can amplify a misleading score.
Deep point searches remain expensive for large-coefficient curves.
evidence_for: The historical record search successfully combined a rank-17 fibration, a sieve score, and point searches.
The new exact mod-2 verifier supplies a cheap final independence certificate once points are found.
approaches.mathematical_family: Algorithmic specialization search across all candidate families.
approaches.missing_lemma: An empirically validated, interpretable filter with materially better cost per additional independent point than the classical score alone.
approaches.predicted_advantage: A measured funnel can redirect compute toward filters that predict actual extra rational points rather than merely high analytic-looking scores.

approaches.blocker: The current reduction ends at a global realization problem that may be comparable to the original challenge.
approaches.central_mechanism: Specify a target Mordell-Weil lattice or a family of modular independence signatures first, then search for elliptic surfaces realizing that combinatorial object.
approaches.computational_cost: Low for combinatorial prototypes; very high for geometric realization and exact section recovery.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Use the exact local E(F_p)/2E(F_p) certificate as a model: design binary signatures for 30 prospective sections with sparse algebraic constraints, then ask which divisor/intersection data on an elliptic surface could realize those signatures compatibly across primes.
evidence_against: Most abstract lattices or modular signatures need not be geometrically realizable by rational sections.
Local compatibility does not imply a global elliptic surface.
No realization theorem currently turns a designed rank-30 signature into a Q-rational curve.
evidence_for: The rank-29 baseline is certified by a full-rank binary local-image matrix, showing that modular independence signatures are compact and exact.
Neron-Severi and Mordell-Weil groups are lattices constrained by explicit intersection theory.
approaches.mathematical_family: Lattice realization, coding theory, modular images, and optimization-driven construction of Mordell-Weil generators.
approaches.missing_lemma: A practical realization theorem or construction map from designed lattice/modular data to an explicit elliptic surface over Q.
approaches.predicted_advantage: Rank 30 becomes a realization problem for a designed object rather than a tail event in a one-parameter specialization distribution.

approaches.blocker: No credible mechanism currently distinguishes 29 as a universal ceiling.
approaches.central_mechanism: Prove rank E(Q) <= 29 uniformly without restrictions on conductor, height, torsion, or family.
approaches.concrete_next_test: None allocated beyond monitoring for a genuinely new universal mechanism; family-specific or conditional bounds are explicitly rejected as resolutions.
evidence_against: No known unconditional universal rank bound of the required form exists.
Current arithmetic-statistical and height methods do not approach a uniform bound of 29 for every curve.
The route is vastly less concrete than constructive discovery.
approaches.mathematical_family: Global theorems applying to every elliptic curve over Q.
approaches.missing_lemma: A universal mechanism strong enough to bound all Mordell-Weil ranks over Q by 29.
approaches.predicted_advantage: Would solve the challenge negatively if achieved.

approaches.blocker: The remaining trisection-orbit catalogue has not yet been converted to compact cover tensors and audited across enough characteristics.
approaches.central_mechanism: The eight split-E8 sections are combined with differences between three trisections on a common cubic cover; a tangent-derived completely split fibre yields four additional independent Mordell-Weil directions.
approaches.computational_cost: Medium for modular cover-equivalence scans; high for exact lifting, height calculations, and simultaneous split-fibre searches.
approaches.concrete_next_test: Tensorize all 1,920 genus-zero trisection orbits, compare their degree-three covers modulo several good primes up to PGL2 source equivalence, lift surviving collisions over Q, and incrementally certify new directions on rational split fibres.
evidence_against: A first completely split fibre supplied only rank 10 or 11 because an additional exact packet relation appeared.
Complete splitting of one common cubic cover does not automatically make every visible trisection difference independent.
Even a generic rank-12 component remains eighteen directions short of the final target unless it can be combined with stronger geometry or several compatible packets.
evidence_for: certificates/small_split_e8_tangent_fibre_exact_rank12_packet.json proves exact subgroup rank 12 by two exact trace relations and a direct plane-cubic finite-reduction certificate modulo 5.
certificates/small_split_e8_tangent_fibre_rank12_sage.json independently reproduces rank 12 after a SageMath 10.9 plane-cubic-to-Weierstrass transformation.
The direct plane-cubic reduction engine reproduces the earlier rank-10 control fibre before certifying the tangent-derived fibre.
approaches.mathematical_family: A split E8 rational elliptic surface equipped with three genus-zero trisection orbits sharing one degree-three cover of the base.
approaches.missing_lemma: A scalable criterion predicting when several cover-equivalent trisection orbits contribute distinct anti-invariant Mordell-Weil directions after specialization.
approaches.predicted_advantage: It raises a controlled rank-8 geometric floor to an explicitly certified rank-12 subgroup and converts the next search into the finite problem of finding more compatible trisection orbits or covers.

objective: Produce an unconditional certificate that an explicit elliptic curve over Q has rank at least 30.

status_definitions.ACTIVE: There is a concrete executable next experiment and no known fatal obstruction.
status_definitions.AUDIT_REQUIRED: A branch or note contains a claim that must be independently rederived before use.
status_definitions.BLOCKED: The route currently terminates in a missing lemma or object comparable in difficulty to the original target.
status_definitions.DEPRIORITIZED: Retained for completeness but not allocated substantial resources under the constructive-first policy.
status_definitions.PROVED_MODULE: A reusable theorem or construction is proved exactly, but it does not by itself solve rank 30.
status_definitions.SCOUTING: The representation is materially distinct but has not yet produced a verified construction.
status_definitions.VERIFIED_BASELINE: The stated result is reproduced by an exact executable certificate.
